title: Karur stampede: a package on the tragedy at Vijay’s TVK rally in Tamil Nadu
content:
During the third leg of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party president and actor Vijay’s State-wide political tour, 41 persons including nine children died in a stampede at a rally addressed by Mr. Vijay at Karur in Tamil Nadu on September 27, 2025 (Saturday).

The meeting, held at Velusamypuram, began at 7:20 p.m. and drew several thousand people who had been packed into congested roads since the morning, waiting to see and hear Mr. Vijay.

As the crowd, mostly youngsters, surged towards the vehicles to see the actor-turned-politician, many people who had been standing at the meeting point since 10 a.m. were forced to move to give way for Mr. Vijay’s vehicle. With very little room left to move, chaos and confusion ensued, triggering a stampede.

Since many people were fainting and sensing that the situation was getting out of control, Mr. Vijay cut his speech short and left the spot, which, by then, resembled a war zone.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin who rushed to Karur Government Hospital in a few hours announced a solatium of ₹10 lakh each to the deceased and ₹1 lakh each to the injured and ordered the constitution of one-woman commission headed by retired High Court judge Aruna Jagadeesan, to probe the incident.

Meanwhile, Mr. Vijay announced a compensation of ₹20 lakh each to the families of those who lost their lives and ₹2 lakh each to those who were injured and undergoing treatment, on behalf of TVK.
summary: Vijay’s State-wide political tour began at 7:20 p.m. During the third leg of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party tour, 41 people including nine children died in a stampede . the party president and actor announced a solatium of 10 lakh each to the deceased and 1 lakh each . 2 lakh each was paid to those who were injured and undergoing treatment .

title: First arrests made after stampede at Vijay's Karur rally, BJP, TVK leaders among three held for spreading rumours
content:
The Chennai Police said on Monday that three people were arrested for spreading rumours about the Karur stampede. The three individuals included:

Sahayam, 38, from Perumbakkam, BJP State Secretary (Art & Culture;) Sivaneswaran from Mangadu, a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) member Sarathkumar, 32, from Avadi, TVK's 46th Ward Secretary Earlier, the three TVK functionaries were booked in connection with the incident. They were the district secretary for Karur North, Mathiazhagan, the party's state general secretary, Bussy Anand, and TVK's deputy general secretary, Nirmal Kumar.

The FIR against them was filed under sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 110 (attempt to commit culpable homicide), 125 (endangering life of others), and 223 (disobedience to order), of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with section 3 of the Tamil Nadu Public Property (Preventing of Damage and Loss) Act, 1992, a police official was quoted by PTI as saying.

The police have not booked any case against actor Vijay.

Karur stampede As many as 41 people died in the stampede at a rally of actor Vijay-led TVK at Velusamypuram in Karur on the evening of September 27.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin on Monday said that political parties and public organisations should frame rules on how public events must be organised responsibly in the future.

"What happened in Karur is a great tragedy; a cruel tragedy! A tragedy that has never happened before; a tragedy that should never happen again. The scenes I witnessed when I personally visited the hospital are still fresh before my eyes. I continue to remain in deep grief and sorrow," Stalin said in a video message posted on his X handle.

Probe launched To ascertain the full and true cause of the tragedy, a one-member Commission of Inquiry headed by former judge Justice Aruna Jagadeesan has been constituted.

"I assure you that the next course of action by the government will be based on the Commission's report," Stalin said.

Meanwhile, Vijay's TVK filed a writ petition in the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Monday, pleading for the transfer of the probe into the recent stampede in Karur from the State police to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

In the writ petition, the TVK alleged that Saturday's "incident was solely motivated by the DMK and its functionaries."

"A petition has been filed before the High Court of Madras, Madurai Bench, seeking a transfer of the case from the Town Police Station of Karur to the Central Investigation Team for a probe into the entire occurrence," Arivazhagan, the advocate for TVK, was quoted by ANI as saying.
summary: a friend died in the stampede at a rally of actor Vijay-led TVK . three people were arrested for spreading rumours about the Karur stampede . police have not booked any case against them . writ petition filed in the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court .

title: Karur stampede: Death toll climbs to 41, probe panel continues inquiry
content:
The toll in the crowd crush at the TVK rally in Karur has risen to 41, with the death of one more person at the Karur Government Medical College and Hospital.

Suguna, 60, was critically injured in the incident, and was admitted to the hospital late on Saturday (September 27, 2025) night. But she did not respond to treatment, and died in the early hours of Monday (September 29).

Also View: A visual timeline on how Karur stampede unfolded

Sources at the hospital said that of the 41 victims, 39 were brought dead on Saturday night. Kavin, who died on Sunday, was first admitted to a private hospital on Saturday and then shifted to the government hospital, where he died.

Collector M. Thangavel said the victims included 18 women, 13 men, five boys, and five girls. Of the 110 people injured, 51 have been discharged, while 60 remain hospitalised — 51 at the Government Medical College and Hospital, two at Amaravathi Hospital, five at Akshaya Hospital, and one at Apollo Hospitals.

Solatium distributed

On Sunday Thoothukudi MP Kanimozhi and Karur MLA V. Senthilbalaji met the families of 18 victims and distributed relief cheques. The State government has announced ₹10 lakh in compensation for each bereaved family and ₹1 lakh for the injured.

Retired High Court judge Aruna Jagadeesan, constituting the one-member Commission of Inquiry, continued her work in Karur on Monday. The commission visited the homes of the victims to gather accounts of the tragedy.

At Emoor Pudur, Ms. Jagadeesan met Sakthivel, who lost his wife Priyadharshini, 35, and daughter Dharanika, 14. She also visited the homes of victims Arukkani, Chandra, and Pruthik, before proceeding to Chinnakkavundanur to meet the family of Kokilasri, 27.

According to the families, the former judge asked questions about how the incident occurred, the number of police personnel deployed, the speed of medical response, and access to ambulances. Residents said they hoped the inquiry would ensure accountability and prevent such tragedies in the future.

The tragedy, which unfolded on Saturday night at Velusamypuram, has triggered grief, political visits, and a closer scrutiny of crowd management at mass events.

Several leaders called on the families of the deceased. Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president K. Selvaperunthagai, along with AICC in-charge for Tamil Nadu Girish Chodankar, conveyed his condolences. Tamizhaga Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam leader John Pandian also met the bereaved families.

CCTV footage being examined

The Karur Town police booked 10 persons who attended the TVK rally for allegedly assaulting a private ambulance driver, Eswaramoorthy of Mariamman Koil Street, on Saturday night. The police said the driver was attempting to ferry victims when his vehicle was blocked. He was admitted to a private hospital after sustaining injuries. CCTV footage from the locality is being examined to identify the attackers.
summary: in the crowd crush at the TVK rally in Karur has risen to 41 . of the 110 people injured, 39 were brought dead on Saturday night . the death of one more person at the Karur Government Medical College and Hospital . 10 lakh in compensation for each bereaved family and 1 lakh for the injured .
